To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we found a new integrable problem of a particle moving on a surface of an ellipsoid in an inverse square field of force.

we have shown that the problem of a particle moving on the surface on an n -dimensioned ellipsoid in a force field with potential energy terms inversely proportional to squares of distances to the (n-1)-dimensioned planes of symmetry is integrable.
the Jacobi problem of a point on an ellipsoid in a field of inverse square force can be solved by separation of variables in elliptic coordinates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following problems.
the problem of a point particle moving on the surface S of an ellipsoid of revolution in an inverse square potential field, which we shall refer to as the ellipsoid billiards problem.
the problem of a point particle moving in a potential field on a curved surface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the case of an ellipsoid, the Jacobi problem of geodesics is integrable in a very general sense.

the integrable billiards and geodesic problems in the space of constant negative curvature are integrable by using elliptic coordinates, and the billiards problems in the space with constant positive curvature are not integrable by using these coordinates.

the problem of a point particle moving on a surface of a constant curvature in the field of a conservative force with a potential proportional to the square of the distance to the plane of symmetry of the surface is integrable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found integrable generalizations of the problem of a point on a surface in a conservative field.
we have obtained new integrable extensions of the Jacobi's Problem on the ellipsoid.
we found a new integrable problem of geodesics in a conservative field on an ellipsoid in a space of constant curvature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of an elliptic potential, Jacobi's problem is integrable in the sense that it has n independent commuting constants of the motion.
the integrals of motion of Jacobi's problem are not unique, and the problem of finding them is a non-trivial problem in itself.

the integrable billiards problems in the elliptic plane are closely related to the problem of geodesics in a space of constant curvature, and that the latter can be reduced to the former by an appropriate choice of variables.
